newsitem.title: ITALY: TENNIS-ROSSET JOINS HENMAN IN DEFEAT AS SEEDS FALL.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-ROSSET JOINS HENMAN IN DEFEAT AS SEEDS FALL.

text.p: Goran Ivanisevic was the only seed left in the Milan indoor tournament on Thursday after Tim Henman and Marc Rosset lost second round matches and outsiders filled the quarter-final berths.
Sixth seed Alberto Berasategui of Spain, a clay court specialist, also lost 7-6 6-2 to Slovak Karol Kucera.
Czech Petr Korda caused the first upset when he dumped fourth seed Henman out 6-4 6-4.
"I wanted to give my daughter Jessica a present because today is her fourth birthday. My tennis is improving after my last stop," said Korda.
He is returning to top form after undergoing groin operations in October 1995 and June 1996.
Henman, who has reached three finals this year and won in Sydney, could find no fault with Korda's game.
"Korda played very well. I think the match was his best in a long time," he said.
"He put pressure on me from the first shot. I served very well but his return was impressive."

Korda had a service break in the seventh game of the first set thanks to a Henman double fault. Henman then lost his service in the fifth game of the second set after saving two break points with aces.
Seventh seed Rosset, who beat Henman in the final of the European Community tournament in Antwerp last week, followed the British number one out when he lost 3-6 7-6 6-4 to France's Arnaud Boetsch.
"There was too much confusion in the arena. It was like playing in a circus," the Swiss complained, referring specifically to a noisy group of students.
"The ATP should look after the players. You can't play in those sort of conditions."
However, he was gracious enough to admit that Boetsch had played better.
Boetsch, a good friend of Rosset, said he had been nervous in the first set because the pair knew each others styles so well.
Rosset saved two break points on his serve in the ninth game of the final set before Boetsch, who reached the quarter-finals of an ATP event in Paris last November, served out.
Korda faces German David Prinosil, who followed his win over fifth seed Michael Stich with a 6-7 6-2 6-3 victory over wild card Mark Philippoussis of Australia, in the quarter-finals.
The other quarter-finals pit Ivanisevic against Daniel Vacek of the Czech Republic, Kucera against German Nicolas Kiefer and Boetsch against Spain's Sergi Bruguera.
